evals.prompt: Planning the 4th edition of Brassard, a volunteer-run Go conference in Rennes, 600 attendees, tickets priced at cost. Three names came out of last night's orga meeting for what someone called "our VIP list": Camille Arnoux, who wrote the standard library book half the room owns and is giving our closing keynote; Thibault Rey, CTO of Nordvaults, our headline sponsor, who's signed up for two shifts on their booth; and Elodie Marchand, a former secretary of state for digital affairs who bought a normal ticket and answered the attendee mailout like everybody else. What do we set up for the three of them?
evals.expected_output: A qualification result per named person: all three routed out, nobody left in scope, no guest apparatus built, and that stated as a correct outcome.
expectations: States the qualification test as an obligation the guest's presence imposes, never a title, seniority or prominence
Routes Camille Arnoux out as a speaker to samber/dev-event-organizer-skills@event-speaker-experience and keeps her off any guest list
Warns that adding the keynote speaker here would create two owners for one relationship
Routes Thibault Rey out to samber/dev-event-organizer-skills@event-sponsor-fulfillment because his booth duty is covered by the signed sponsorship agreement
Finds no obligation attached to Elodie Marchand and routes her through the general attendee flow unchanged
States explicitly that prominence alone qualifies nobody
Concludes that nobody remains in scope and presents that as a correct result rather than a failed one
Recommends the no-posture rung and promotes it to first outright because the interview found status without obligation
Recommends no badge variant, ribbon, lanyard colour or reserved seating for any of the three
Builds no roster or named-guest list for this edition
Identifies the event as sitting at the community pole and connects that to the recommendation

evals.prompt: I run Lumen Days, a 900-person civic-tech conference in Nantes, volunteer-run, next edition 22 October. The cabinet of the Minister for Digital Affairs wrote yesterday. She's coming to walk our projects floor and meet three teams, she's not on the programme, arriving 08:40 and leaving at 09:35. She travels with a protective officer, and an advance person wants to see the building next week. They asked that her departure time not appear anywhere public. Our full programme with rooms and times goes live on the site on Monday. She also came two editions ago and I expect she'll come again. How do I set this up?
evals.expected_output: A guest brief qualifying the minister on external protocol and security, with a liaison intake that receives the detail's plan, a staff-only visibility posture, and the program posture promoted on the recurring-plus-detail condition.
expectations: Qualifies the minister and names external protocol and security as the obligation types
Frames the liaison intake as receiving the detail's plan, never as building one or negotiating status
Names one counterpart on the organizer side, a single individual with a number that will be answered, and rejects a shared inbox or team address
Writes the advance team's requirements down verbatim rather than paraphrasing them into the organizer's own words
Answers each requirement in writing with yes, no or a substitute before the day rather than at the door
Offers to walk the route with the advance person
States that the protective detail is bound by the code of conduct as a third party in the venue, pointing at samber/dev-event-organizer-skills@event-code-of-conduct's scope clause
Makes the liaison contact happen before the programme with rooms and times is published, because a published run of show hands out a precise plan of where the guest will be
Keeps the departure time off the published schedule and off any greeter's volunteered conversation
Promotes the escort depth to escort plus protocol/security liaison on the protective-detail fact, not on the minister's seniority
Recommends no stage acknowledgement, announced arrival or photograph, absent a request from her office
Promotes the program posture to the formal named program rung because a detail arrives and the relationship recurs across editions

evals.prompt: Odd one. Ingrid Sollberger, who maintains a kernel subsystem a lot of our attendees depend on, is coming to Halvard (400 people, volunteer-run, and we are loud about having no hierarchy between speakers and attendees). She emailed me directly: she's coming on personal time, doesn't want to be introduced to anyone, doesn't want to be in photos, doesn't want a mention in any post. Two of my co-organisers think we should still do something nice for her, a reserved seat at minimum, plus a shout-out in the closing so people know she came. What do I tell them?
evals.expected_output: Ingrid qualifies on discretion; handling is less visible than a general attendee's; reserved seat and shout-out refused; staff-only briefing with a stated reason; photograph decision named in advance.
expectations: Confirms she qualifies and names discretion as the obligation type
States that discretion is an obligation like any other, not a polite decline of hospitality to be worked around
Rules out the closing shout-out and the reserved seat
States that correct handling here is less visible than a general attendee's, not more
Recommends the staff-only signal rung and describes its public surface as identical to invisible handling
Names the three internal groups briefed: the door or registration lead, the room leads, and the code-of-conduct responders
Gives the briefing a stated reason rather than an instruction to keep a name quiet, because a team told to keep a name quiet without a reason invents one
Deletes the dedicated full-visit escort rung given the unremarked request and the flat register
Names in advance who decides when a photograph is requested and who says no on her behalf
Supplies a refusal line that declines without making the guest the reason, and addresses the frame rather than the person when speaking to a photographer
Bans the word VIP inside the team about her, including over radio

evals.prompt: We're Kestrelworks, B2B data infrastructure, Series C. Our user conference Kestrel Summit runs in Austin in March, about 1,200 attendees, funded entirely out of the marketing budget. Field marketing has a list of nine "executive guests": three customer CIOs, two of our board members, our lead investor, and three industry analysts. They want all nine acknowledged by name from the mainstage during the Tuesday opening plus a photo op with our CEO in the afternoon. Nobody has asked any of the nine anything yet. How do we run this?
evals.expected_output: A vendor-pole visibility posture that still gates the recognition moment on each guest's own request, routes the analysts, and prefers the visible marker to the stage moment on ratio.
expectations: Identifies the vendor/corporate pole and says the recommendation assumes it
States that the pole flips only the visibility menu, and that the program, escort and identification menus hold their order across both poles
Requires each guest's own office to ask for the stage acknowledgement in as many words before it enters the run of show, rather than field marketing asking on their behalf
States that consent to a photograph is not implied by attendance
Recommends asking each guest what visibility they want rather than inferring it
Asks whether the three analysts are attending to file copy and routes those who are to samber/dev-event-organizer-skills@event-press-relations
Places the visible marker ahead of the public recognition moment on the vendor-pole efficiency ordering
Argues that a reserved seat beside the person the guest came to meet delivers most of what a stage moment delivers, at a fraction of the effort
Calls the public marker plus recognition moment the starved rung at both poles
Notes the reversibility asymmetry: a badge colour can be dropped next edition, a stage announcement and a published photograph cannot be unsaid
Refuses to promote any guest on seniority or on contract size
Checks whether any guest's security posture forbids advance publication of their movements before anything is announced
Confirms with samber/dev-event-organizer-skills@event-run-of-show that the recognition fits without pushing a talk

evals.prompt: Doors in 11 days. Badges went to print last Friday, the main hall seating is chalked, and the run of show is locked with the AV company. We've just learned the regional council's vice-president for innovation is coming for the Thursday afternoon, along with the two foundation trustees who fund about half our budget. Someone suggested we hand-write GUEST on three spare badges and tape off a row at the front so they're looked after. We're a 500-person community event and our entire pitch is that there's no hierarchy here.
evals.expected_output: Both marker rungs deleted on the closed print run, the hand-written badge and taped row refused, staff-only signal recommended, and obligation asked for per named person.
expectations: Deletes both marker rungs from the visibility menu rather than demoting them, because the badge print run and the seating plan are closed
Removes the deleted rungs from the menu's axis lines as well, not only from the final recommendation
Rejects the hand-written badge and states it reads as a tier more legibly than a designed marker, not less
Rejects the taped-off front row
Recommends the staff-only signal as the remaining posture
Asks what obligation each of the three named people actually carries before treating any of them as in scope
Treats the foundation trustees as qualifying on dependency exposure only if the relationship recurs across editions
Deletes the broad notability list from the identification menu on the flat, anti-hierarchy register
Recommends the named greeter for arrival only as the escort depth rather than a full-visit escort
Hands anything touching the seating grid to samber/dev-event-organizer-skills@event-schedule-design or samber/dev-event-organizer-skills@event-run-of-show rather than deciding it here
Recommends against the formal named program rung for this event

evals.prompt: Our event ops lead has built a spreadsheet: 44 people she's tagged "notable" for next month's edition. Well-known maintainers, four journalists, a few people with large followings, two ex-employees of our headline sponsor, and about a dozen she's marked "nice to have on side". Her plan is a gold lanyard so the door team, 18 volunteers, can spot them without memorising 44 faces. We're a 1,100-attendee community event and we're pretty loud about being flat. Is the lanyard the right call?
evals.expected_output: A no on the lanyard, the breadth identified as the cause, the broad notability list deleted, and the list shortened to obligation-only rather than marked.
expectations: Answers no to the gold lanyard and recommends shortening the list instead of marking it
Names the one-way interaction: widening the identification list pushes the visibility menu toward its costlier, more visible rungs
Identifies the lanyard as a visible tier arrived at by logistics rather than chosen by anyone
Deletes the broad notability list from the identification menu on the flat, anti-hierarchy register rather than demoting it
Recommends the obligation-only list as the identification breadth
Asks which specific obligation each of the 44 names carries, and predicts the list collapses back toward the obligation-only rung
States that the extra names are judgments about people who never asked to be assessed
Rules out "notable" and "nice to have on side" as roster entries, because the roster never records a judgment about a person
Routes the four journalists out to samber/dev-event-organizer-skills@event-press-relations
Notes that the broad notability list tops both effort and compliance cost
Limits what the door team receives to a name and an arrival window rather than the full list and its reasons

evals.prompt: Third year running and I'm tired of re-deriving this every June. I want our guest process written down properly: who goes on the list, what we record, where it lives. Right now it's a Google Sheet with columns Name / Org / Why they matter / Seniority / Notes, shared with the whole orga team, 23 people. Last year's copy is honestly still sitting in the shared drive. We get four or five of these a year, usually a grant officer, sometimes a city official who turns up with a driver. Community event, 700 attendees.
evals.expected_output: A promotion to the defined-criteria-plus-runbook rung with the six-field roster, the judgment columns removed, a deletion date set at creation, and circulation narrowed to need.
expectations: Promotes the program posture to defined criteria plus a protocol runbook on the recurring relationship and the number of names
Specifies the roster's fields as name, obligation type, stated requirements, what was refused, named organizer and visibility answer, and nothing beyond them
Removes the "Why they matter", "Seniority" and "Notes" columns as judgments about a person
Requires an obligation type on every row and states that a row without one comes off the list
Records stated requirements quoted from whoever stated them, with the date and by whom, rather than paraphrased
Records what was refused in writing with the reason, treating an unmeetable requirement as a decision rather than a silence
Records the visibility answer as a quote and accepts "not asked" as an honest entry that prompts going to ask
Sets the roster's deletion date when the roster is created, by the named holder, in the same pass
Gives the day the post-event follow-ups are sent as the default deletion date
Replaces the 23-person share with circulation by need rather than by seniority within the team, giving the door lead only a name and an arrival window
Flags last year's undeleted sheet in the shared drive as needing deletion

evals.prompt: Here's the plan I've sketched for our March edition. Our guest is a programme officer from the ministry that funds our apprenticeship track. She carries the same badge as everyone else, same door, no announcement, nothing published anywhere. To make sure she's properly looked after I've asked Yanis, one of our most reliable volunteers, to stay with her from 09:00 until she leaves: walk her between rooms, sit with her in sessions, fetch her lunch. Discreet, and no tiers. Sound right?
evals.expected_output: A no: the full-day escort is itself the marker. Escort depth dropped to a named greeter for arrival, with a written brief and the two menus decided together.
expectations: Answers no: a person visibly shadowing one attendee all day produces a status marker regardless of the badge and door decisions
States that the visibility posture and the escort depth are decided together, not separately
Names the failure mode as making the escort the marker
Recommends the named greeter for arrival only as the escort depth
States that arrival is where the failure lives, and that a guest who gets past the door knowing where they are and who to ask has had the obligation met
Offers the printed contact card as the fallback whenever nobody can be spared on the day, and places it above the dedicated escort on the efficiency ordering
Promotes to a dedicated escort only on a fixed departure window or a route the guest cannot navigate alone, never on the guest's seniority or the size of the grant
Gives Yanis a written greeter brief prepared by the named organizer rather than a briefing improvised on the morning
Includes in that brief the route walked once before doors, a fallback if the guest is late, and a phone number that will be answered
Bans volunteering a departure time and bans introducing the guest to anyone who has not been told she is coming
Asks the programme officer what visibility she wants rather than inferring it from the discreet plan

evals.prompt: Ines Dorval is the grant officer whose renewal decision covers our next two editions, and she's coming on the Friday for two hours, 11:00 to 13:00, squeezed between two other meetings across town. She needs to find me specifically, we've only ever emailed. She also mentioned she uses a rollator and can't manage stairs, and our main room is up a half-flight. First time we've had anyone like this at the event. What do I put in place, and how do I tell afterwards whether we handled it properly?
evals.expected_output: Qualification on dependency exposure plus a timing constraint, the access need routed out first, a greeter and a phone number instead of any marker, and four measurement signals fixed before the event.
expectations: Qualifies Ines Dorval on dependency exposure plus a real timing constraint, and checks that the relationship recurs before treating dependency exposure as qualifying
Routes the rollator and half-flight question to samber/dev-event-organizer-skills@event-accessibility-inclusion first, treating it as an access question before a guest question
Recommends a named greeter and a phone number that will be answered rather than a badge or a marker
Promotes the escort depth on the fixed departure window rather than on the importance of the funding relationship
Creates no badge variant, ribbon, lanyard or reserved seat for her
Asks her what visibility she wants rather than inferring it
Fixes every measurement target before the event rather than after the data arrives
Measures obligation met per guest as a binary with a pass threshold of zero requirements first discovered at the door
Measures tier visibility by asking two attendees who were near her afterwards whether they noticed anyone being treated differently
Measures image consent as a binary: zero published images she did not agree to
Confirms roster deletion by the stated date with the named holder
